previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with suprapubic pain and a history of chronic indwelling Foley catheter use due to hypotonic bladder. He had recently undergone a catheter change due to poor drainage and developed severe lower abdominal pain two days prior to presentation. Initial concern was for a symptomatic UTI given his history of multidrug-resistant organisms, including ESBL-producing E. coli. He was started on intravenous Zosyn and admitted for monitoring. However, after evaluation by Infectious Disease and urology, his symptoms were attributed to catheter-induced bladder irritation rather than active infection. The antibiotics were discontinued, and he was managed conservatively. A yeast infection of the penis was identified and treated with topical antifungal cream. The patient was discharged home with home services, continuing his baseline medications and a bowel regimen, with instructions to secure his catheter bag properly and follow up with urology to discuss long-term management options, including a possible suprapubic catheter.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Hypoxia, question fluid overload or pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  AP upright and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  Midline
sternotomy wires and mediastinal clips are compatible with prior CABG.  There
is interval development of right basilar opacity which is likely secondary to
atelectasis (RML and RLL).  Underlying pneumonia cannot be entirely excluded. 
The left lung is clear though low lung volumes somewhat limit the evaluation.

IMPRESSION:  Right basilar opacity likely atelectasis though pneumonia cannot
be excluded.
